dhp33:2: difficult to guard, difficult to ward,
dhp33:4: as a fletcher does his arrow.
dhp34:1: Like a fish thrown up on dry land,
dhp34:2: pulled out from its watery home,
dhp34:4: (one ought) to throw off the sway of Māra.
dhp35:1: * For the mind that is difficult to subdue, flighty, flitting wherever it will,
dhp36:1: Hard to see, very subtle, flitting wherever it will,
dhp36:3: the sage should guard the mind,
dhp37:1: * Those who will restrain the mind that roams far,
dhp37:4: is lonesome, without a body, hidden, gain release from the bonds of Māra.
dhp38:1: For the one with unsettled mind,
dhp38:2: who does not know the True Dhamma,
dhp39:1: For the one with mind free of lust,
dhp39:2: for the one with mind unperplexed,
dhp39:3: for the one who has abandoned making merit and demerit, for the watchful, there is no fear.
dhp40:1: Knowing this body is (frail) like a jar,
dhp40:2: establishing the mind like a fortress,
dhp40:3: fight Māra with the weapon of wisdom,
dhp40:4: guard your success, and do not be attached.
dhp41:1: Before long has passed by, alas, this body will lie on the ground,
dhp41:4: just like a useless piece of wood.
dhp42:1: Whatever an aggressor might do to an aggressor,
dhp42:2: or an enemy to an enemy –
dhp42:3: a mind that is badly-directed can do far worse than that to him.
dhp43:1: Mother and father might not do for him,
dhp43:3: as much good as a mind that is well-directed can do for him.
